title: Sell Mineral Rights in Johnstown, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Johnstown, CO | Weld-Larimer DJ Basin
metaDescription: Own minerals near Johnstown, straddling the Weld-Larimer county line in the Wattenberg field? We price your interest off real decline data.
heroLead: Johnstown sits right on the Weld-Larimer county line, one of the fastest-growing towns along the Front Range, which puts mineral ownership here at the intersection of active drilling and expanding subdivisions.
intro: As Johnstown has grown, local and county setback requirements for new wells near occupied structures have become more conservative than they were a decade ago, which has generally slowed how quickly new permits move forward close to town, without affecting production from units already established.
For owners, that means the timeline for an unleased tract near newer development can look quite different than for a tract already inside a long-established Wattenberg unit.

sections.heading: Producing units near Johnstown
paragraphs: Wells already drilled and online continue paying under their existing unit agreements regardless of subsequent growth nearby. We price these off a standard decline curve applied to your trailing production.

sections.heading: Growth and setback timelines
paragraphs: For acreage that has not yet been leased, proximity to Johnstown's expanding subdivisions means any future well would need to satisfy tighter setback and safety requirements than a rural location, which can extend permitting timelines.

sections.heading: Straddling two counties
paragraphs: Because Johnstown sits across the Weld-Larimer line, we confirm which county's records and, where relevant, which jurisdiction's rules apply to your specific parcel before finalizing title and pricing.

sections.heading: What growth means for existing royalty income
paragraphs: Owners sometimes worry that residential growth near Johnstown will somehow reduce their existing royalty income. It will not. A well already producing continues under its existing unit agreement regardless of what gets built nearby; growth mainly affects whether and how quickly new, separate wells get permitted.

faqs.question: Does Johnstown's rapid growth affect my producing interest?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Existing production prices off its decline curve regardless of nearby residential growth.

faqs.question: Why might a new well near Johnstown take longer to permit than it used to?
faqs.answer: Growing residential development nearby means stricter setback and safety requirements apply, which can slow new permitting timelines.

faqs.question: How do you handle a parcel that sits on the Weld-Larimer county line?
faqs.answer: We confirm the correct county records and jurisdiction for your specific legal description before finalizing anything.

faqs.question: Will nearby home construction reduce my current royalty payments?
faqs.answer: No, existing production continues under its established unit agreement regardless of nearby development. Growth mainly affects new permitting, not existing wells.

faqs.question: How do you decide which county's office to pull records from for a boundary-line parcel?
faqs.answer: We check the legal description against both Weld and Larimer County recording systems and confirm which one actually holds the parcel of record before starting title work.
